subject: Catalyst pilot SOW - warranty/indemnity and pricing questions
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin@catalysthealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@catalysthealth.com
Date: 2026-11-13T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot SOW questions — warranty, indemnity, liability cap

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for sending the latest SOW (v3). Procurement and legal at Catalyst ran a quick review and we have three stickier items before we can sign the pilot order:

1) Liability cap — the SOW currently references Redwood’s standard cap. For a regulated pilot touching PHI-adjacent telemetry we need a higher cap tied to fees (we proposed 6 months of fees in our redline).

2) Indemnity — the redlines ask for broader customer indemnity carveouts (IP and data-related claims). Our legal team wants to ensure warranty and indemnity are mutual for third-party IP claims.

3) Warranty period / data-loss warranty — Catalyst is asking for a limited warranty on data handling and a specific remediation commitment for any data integrity incidents.

We also flagged pricing — the pilot spend is meaningful for them and procurement has requested a one-time pilot discount (they suggested 20% off list for the initial 6 months).

I attached our annotated SOW (Catalyst_SOW_v3.pdf) and the procurement redline for your review. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept any of these (or propose alternatives)? If you need exec authorization for any of the legal concessions, please let us know the expected timeline — Catalyst would like to pilot in January.

Appreciate your quick take.

— Erin Walsh
Head of Procurement | Catalyst Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot SOW questions — warranty, indemnity, liability cap

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I’ve looped in Legal (Laura) and Deal Desk (Jordan) to scope what we can concede without exec review and what will need escalation.

Quick thoughts:
- Liability cap: this is likely an exec-level exception for a regulated data-touching pilot.
- Indemnity: Legal will propose mutually acceptable language; some customers ask for mutual IP indemnity, which we can consider with limits.
- Warranty: we can offer a narrowly scoped data-integrity warranty but will want precise incident/threshold definitions and a remediation SLA.

I’m going to request a recommended redline and an explicit approval ask from Legal. Jordan — can you weigh in on pricing tradeoffs? Erin — would you prefer we schedule a short call this week to walk through options (30 min)?

I’ll circulate a candidate approval package once Legal sends recommended language.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SOW questions — recommended redlines and exec ask

Marcus / Jordan / Jonas — I reviewed Catalyst's redlines and the attached SOW. Summary and recommended positions below (legal rationale included).

Summary of Catalyst requests:
- Liability cap tied to fees (Catalyst suggested 6 months fees) and higher absolute exposure for data-related incidents.
- Broader customer-favorable indemnity language (including third-party IP claims).
- Specific warranty on data handling plus a remediation commitment.

Recommended Redwood positions (three-tier approach):
1) Operational (no exec needed):
   - Accept a 90-day warranty window limited to breach of service commitments and demonstrable data corruption tied to our delivery.
   - Add a remediation SLA (investigation + 30-day remediation plan) for data integrity incidents.

2) Deal Desk approval (Jordan):
   - One-time pilot discount up to 18% for a 6-month pilot (with clause that subsequent renewal is at list or mutually agreed rates).
   - Add a DPA amendment for PHI-adjacent handling that tightens controls (standard template).

3) Exec-level approval required (Jonas / C-suite):
   - Increase liability cap to $750,000 for the pilot term or alternatively 9 months of fees, whichever is higher. This is a non-standard exposure for Redwood and requires explicit exec sign-off.
   - Mutual indemnity for third-party IP claims but with carveouts and a $1M aggregate cap across IP indemnity during the pilot; again, exec exception.

Legal notes:
- We should avoid unlimited indemnity for data claims. Any higher cap must be paired with strong contractual limits (e.g., single-incident carveouts, cooperation obligations, cyber insurance requirement).
- Recommend a condition precedent: Catalyst must provide evidence of cyber insurance (minimum $2M) and acknowledge the pilot is for evaluation only (limits on remedial damages).

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a tracked-redline (redlines_catalyst_v3.docx) with exact language. I also drafted the Exec Approval memo (pricing_summary_Catalyst.xlsx includes financial impact).

Exec ask (concrete):
- Approve the liability cap increase to $750,000 for the 6-month pilot (or 9 months of fees, whichever is greater).
- Approve mutual IP indemnity limited to $1,000,000 aggregate for pilot period.
- Approve a one-time 18% pilot discount.

If approved, Legal will package final SOW + sign-off memo for signature. If Execs prefer a lower cap, we can propose $500k plus a stronger limitation on consequential damages and a higher discount offset.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Erin Walsh <erin@catalysthealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T08:32:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot SOW questions — exec approval requested (summary & decision options)

Jordan / Jonas — forwarding Laura’s assessment and the customer ask. TL;DR: Catalyst will commit to a 6-month paid pilot if we make limited concessions on cap/indemnity and give a pilot discount. They need decisions to move procurement.

Options for sign-off (pick one and I’ll coordinate final redlines and signature flow):
A) Full concession (recommended by customer):
   - Cap: $750k for pilot OR 9 months fees (whichever greater)
   - IP indemnity: mutual, $1M aggregate pilot cap
   - Discount: 18% one-time for pilot term
   - Conditions: Proof of cyber insurance ($2M), DPA in place

B) Compromise (lower exec exposure):
   - Cap: $500k for pilot
   - IP indemnity: mutual but $500k cap and Redwood exclusion for known third-party claims
   - Discount: 12%

C) Walk-away / push back:
   - Maintain standard cap and indemnity; offer 10% discount and extended proof-of-concept SLA instead of financial concessions.

Business impact: Catalyst is a high-priority pilot account (strong reference potential in health vertical). The 18% discount + $750k exposure would increase short-term commercial risk but materially improve chance of conversion and regional market credibility. Pricing impact in spreadsheet.

Please approve A or B (or suggest modifications). If we get a yes, Legal will finalize redlines and I’ll circulate for signature. Erin — looping you so Catalyst sees timeline expectations.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
